meta.scope: Token and theme support only. This is NOT a mobile component library: no components, no gesture handling, no SwiftUI or Compose adapter, and no device QA has been performed.

conversions.dimension: Core px is a logical reference unit. The native adapter emits the bare number as dp/pt (React Native treats numeric dims as density-independent).
conversions.fontSize: Logical size in dp/pt. Runtime OS text scaling still applies through allowFontScaling (default true); a numeric token cannot promise identical rendered size across devices.
conversions.lineHeight: Computed as round(fontSize * ratio) because React Native wants a length, not a ratio.
conversions.fontWeight: Emitted as a string ('400' | '500' | '600') because that is what React Native accepts.
conversions.cubicBezier: Emitted as {x1,y1,x2,y2}. The consumer must call Easing.bezier(x1,y1,x2,y2); the adapter does not import react-native.
conversions.shadow: Structured layers are kept. React Native has shadowColor/shadowOffset{width,height}/shadowOpacity/shadowRadius on iOS and elevation on Android. CSS spread has no lossless equivalent, so spread is reported in unsupportedFields rather than silently dropped. Elevation approximation is NOT pixel parity.

unsupportedFields: multiple simultaneous shadow layers (React Native applies one shadow per view; nest views or choose one layer)
border width shorthand (consume border.hairline/strong per side)

system-sans.note: Leave fontFamily unset so the platform picks its own UI font: iOS San Francisco, Android Roboto. A comma-separated CSS stack must never appear here.

system-mono.note: React Native has no cross-platform default mono family, so the consumer chooses with Platform.select. The adapter exports this map rather than importing Platform.
